candidate_text: PawLedger is a local-first dog training workspace. Core lanes are Assess, Train, and Review. It prioritizes humane training, privacy, explainable plans, and repeatable progress tracking.
Core entities are DogProfile, HandlerProfile, TrainingGoal, and SessionLog. These support PawLedger lanes and remain local-first.
Persistence uses SQLite with UTC timestamps, migration_version, soft_delete, and deterministic IDs. It stores DogProfile, HandlerProfile, TrainingGoal, and SessionLog without cloud identity.
PawLedger uses a local passcode, no cloud accounts, and optional encrypted export while preserving local SQLite storage.
Assess uses BehaviorRubric with severity 1-5, triggers, reinforcers, and thresholds tied to DogProfile and TrainingGoal.
Train creates TrainingPlan objects composed of Exercise, Criteria, SafetyNote, and a 7-day microcycle using positive reinforcement and BehaviorRubric details.
Training sessions use SessionState values queued, running, paused, completed, and abandoned. They link to TrainingPlan and SessionLog.
Sessions track RewardLedger entries with reward type and reward latency. RewardRecoveryProfile captures reinforcer and recovery patterns for Review.
ReminderPolicy uses quiet hours, timezone-aware local notifications, and a no nagging rule to support TrainingPlan adherence without cloud push.
Review uses ProgressSnapshot to track weekly trends, adherence, and criteria success using SessionState, RewardLedger, RewardRecoveryProfile, and ReminderPolicy.
Multi-dog support uses Household, DogMembership, and HandlerRole. Prevent data mixing between DogProfile records.
Safety boundaries include VetReferral, never diagnose, unsafe_to_continue, and professional trainer guidance. SafetyNote appears when thresholds or severity indicate risk.
Make outputs include TrainingCard, SessionSummary, ProgressSummary, long-form plans, and short-form cards while preserving SafetyNote, positive reinforcement, and never diagnose boundaries.
Import/export uses portable JSONL with schema version and ImportExportManifest, preserving migration_version, soft_delete, encrypted export, Household, DogProfile, and progress history.
Mobile-first UX routes are Dogs tab, Plan tab, Session tab, Progress tab, and Library tab. They map to Assess, Train, Review, and Make outputs.
Complex cases include rescue dog profile, multiple handlers, reactive threshold, and cooldown period. These respect Household, HandlerRole, BehaviorRubric, VetReferral, and unsafe_to_continue.
Testing uses scenario fixtures and deterministic seeds. It covers state transitions, privacy tests, import/export tests, safety boundary tests, multi-dog household behavior, and progress review.
ForageSourcePolicy prefers trusted sources with source freshness and a citation trail. It rejects dominance theory and unsafe punishment advice.
Context layering separates global memory, scoped memory, retrieved evidence, and task-local context. Promotion and pruning rules decide durable knowledge versus task noise.
Final build plan should sequence PawLedger implementation across persistence, domain model, Assess, Train, Review, Make, import/export, safety boundaries, source policy, tests, and UX routes.
Architecture refactor introduces modular service boundaries with lane contract tests and backward-compatible interfaces, preserving existing lane behavior and safety rules.
CrossLaneInsight links Assess, Train, and Review through shared goal state and synchronized lane updates without violating prior architecture constraints.
Migration strategy preserves legacy schema compatibility via backfill script, invariant checks, and a rollback plan aligned with prior migration and privacy policies.
Offline import/export now covers partial import recovery, idempotent replay, and deterministic conflict resolution while keeping encrypted local export guarantees.
Safety-sensitive handling adds explicit escalation protocol, high-risk interruption flow, and veterinary escalation triggers while preserving humane non-diagnostic boundaries.
Documentation package now includes ADR-style architecture records, operator runbook, and model boundary notes with traceable links to prior decisions.
Testing expansion adds cross-module integration coverage, migration matrix checks, and regression guardrails mapped to prior feature and safety decisions.
Regression debugging now follows triage protocol, conflict resolver rules, and a root-cause log tied to decision drift audits and regression tests.
Release readiness now includes explicit checklist, known limitations register, and go/no-go criteria with risk logging across safety and privacy boundaries.
Final handoff roadmap defines phased milestones, acceptance criteria, and post-release validation while preserving full-system continuity and safety constraints.
